steps.name: Newsboy's Voice
steps.text: Extra! Extra! Read all about it!

steps.name: Newsboy's Voice
steps.text: The Victorians are retreating, not fighting!

steps.name: Newsboy's Voice
steps.text: Tara has gotten back all its territory!

steps.name: Newsboy's Voice
steps.text: Peace will be restored to all of Tara by Samhain!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Stop the cart.

steps.name: Soldier's Voice
steps.text: I've been ordered to escort you directly to meet Her Highness, with no delays.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Before I meet her, I need to see it with my own eyes—my sister's city, post-war Tara, the survivors and civilians—have their new lives finally begun?

steps.name: Soldier's Voice
steps.text: ...If you insist.

steps.name: Soldier's Voice
steps.text: But the people are not yet prepared for two red dragons—

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Of course I know that.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Just—just take these!

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: These knives, axes, and bowls are all made of iron. They'll make for good materials.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I beg you, Culann, take them... even if you have to melt them down and make some eyes for our statue.

a.text: Autumn is almost over, and mornings in Na Saoirsí are cold and damp.
A pair of scarred, weathered hands rub against the cold and dry metal goods—much like a soldier running their fingers over a medal of valor in wartime.
The people yell out his name, hoping the broken tools in their hands will be accepted, smelted, and used by the hero to forge the statue.
The hero... yes, the hero... Every story needs a hero like that.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Theo! Theo! Come help carry this stuff into the workshop.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I mean now, Theo! I'll help you sharpen your knife tonight.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: What a lazy brat. This is what you get for pampering him too much.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: No, uh, I mean, doesn't matter if that boy's around, just take everything, please!

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: I can't take everything. We all need these tools to get by. And that goes double for your prosthetic leg.

spans.text: . We all need these tools to get by. And that goes double for your prosthetic leg.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I'm standing up fine, aren't I?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: That wooden leg Nemos made is only temporary. Once better craftsmen arrive in town, they can repair your iron one.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: But you're making a statue to commemorate our victory in the war—one that'll be displayed in the main square during Samhain!

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Frankly, it'd be an honor for my rusty old leg to be a part of that.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: No means no.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Just take it, already. It's all old stuff we'd have thrown out while cleaning anyway—no one's got any use for them.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: What's wrong with these bowls? They look perfectly fine to me.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: We can use clay ones instead. As for the axes, we'll just share the few we've got left.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: The war just ended, and the city's short on everything. If we don't help you, how will the statue ever be finished?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Still, I can't accept used prosthetics, no matter what.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: You're a great man, my hero, but you can be so stubborn!
Loughshinny slowly walks into the crowd.
For some reason, she feels as though there's something separating her from them. As if she's looking at them from the other side of a bonfire.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Excuse me, what are you all doing?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: A new face in town? Haven't seen many of those lately! Where are you from, Vouivre?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I've returned to Tara from a place far, far away.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: See, Culann? If you'd just taken everything without a fuss, you wouldn't have embarrassed yourself in front of our countryman from afar.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: My answer is still no. Not the prosthetic leg. The other stuff... fine.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Why are people donating their pots, pans, and prosthetics?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Because we all want to erect a statue in the square for Samhain, to celebrate Tara's rebirth.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: It's to celebrate Samhain?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I've only ever come across the festival in Taran folklore. It's held after the autumn harvest and before winter, yes? And it's meant to connect this shore to the next.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: You know your stuff, Vouivre!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: We used to just celebrate the harvest every year. It was the Dublinners who told us about the festival's historical origins.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: So we sweep our houses, prepare feasts for our guests, and most importantly, light bonfires! On the day when life and death intertwine, we welcome all visitors to the banquet... There's so much to do!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: And since this is the first Samhain since Tara's rebirth, it should be even more grand.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Good thing, too. Otherwise, Culann would never accept our old pots even if he had to tear down his own house instead.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Speaking of, do you have any iron of your own you'd like to donate, so the hero can add it to the statue?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: All I have on me is a bookmark. I think it's made of iron. Will that do?

spans.text: All I have on me is a bookmark. I
it's made of iron. Will that do?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: You don't need to listen to her, Taran from afar.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: So what sort of statue are you making?

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: A red dragon, to celebrate Tara's rebirth.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: A red dragon...

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I'm telling you, Culann, if you don't take my prosthetic leg, I—I won't leave until you do!

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Then I suppose I'll have to pick you up and carry you back myself.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Ugh! You and your gigantic muscles! By the time Samhain is over and the statue has been erected, we'll all be living the good life. We'll be able to make as many prosthetics as we want!

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Just imagine: a massive dragon statue standing tall in the night. Even through winter, its flames will remain lit, just like in the legends. Why it'd be enough to drive off the man-eating mist...

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: And we wouldn't have to obey that blasted curfew anymore—

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: The curfew is an order approved by the Red Dragon, put in place to ensure our safety.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I know that. Of course I know that!
As they speak, more and more people begin to gather around them, until the alley is completely blocked. They each carry all manner of things meant to be melted down for the statue.
Culann patiently receives each new visitor as the objects at his feet begin to pile up. He's quite a large man, but even he can't carry all of them at once.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Allow me to help you, Culann.

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: Oh, no need for that. My apprentice, Theo—

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Can you really count on Theo, though? We have no idea where that rascal ran off to! He talks a good game, but slacks off when no one's watching—typical Victorian!

steps.name: Culann
steps.text: And how old was he when his parents died? Does he even remember Victoria?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: So what's your name, friend?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Reed.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Have you found a place to stay yet? You're welcome to stay at my place for the night—you wouldn't want to be wandering the streets during curfew, that's for sure.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I think I do. But... a curfew? You mean the city has a lights-out bell?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Not quite. Victoria used lights-out bells to suppress the Tarans. Na Saoirsí's curfew is to safeguard us.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: The black mist lingers in the Dark Woods, shielding all of Na Saoirsí from outsiders, but at times, it also drifts into the city streets.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: The curfew is meant to prevent anyone from encountering the mist. It permits no trespass—anyone who enters without permission will never return.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: You mean the mist really eats people?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: ...Listen to yourself. You come all this way, and this is what you ask about? Look, things will be better soon, just you wait.

spans.text: ...Listen to yourself. You come all this way, and
is what you ask about? Look, things will be better soon, just you wait.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Now come with me. I'll show you around Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What about the man building the statue? Culann, was it? What is he going to do? I know a bit of Arts. Perhaps I could help him.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Oh, don't worry about him! He's a genuine hero! He once dispatched an entire Victorian scout team in the Dark Woods. Unfortunately, he was a bit of a softy at the last moment. He's the only one willing to put up with Theo's nonsense.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: All by himself? Really?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Well, in the woods. The forest has always been on the Tarans' side—Ugh! Stop changing the subject, Reed!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Just come with me and have some ale and stewed meat. It'll warm you right up!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: You must know that you've come home at the perfect time.
Phew. Well, at least there are still potatoes in the store...
Damn! Look at the time! I'm late!

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Who's the one charging through here like a wrecking ball—?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Theo?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Sorry, sorry. I'm just in a hurry to get back. I didn't mean to bump into you, sir. Here. Let me wipe that off for you.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: ...You dare to disrespect me, too?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: What? No, no. Maybe I misspoke. I was just wondering if you needed help—

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Stay away from me!
The man raises his cane and strikes Theo hard on the chest, knocking him away.
The morning mist has long since gathered in the uneven crevices of the stone pavement, forming murky puddles. Caught off guard, Theo stumbles backward and falls straight into one.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: You Victorian scoundrel! Who do you think you are? How dare you offer me charity?!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Urgh...!
Put that cane away! What's going on here?
Are you okay, Theo?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I'm fine, Brigid, I'm fine. I crashed into him first.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: A rootless nomad and a Victorian mongrel—couldn't ask for a more perfect pair of lowlives.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: You're not exactly making your ancestors proud, Brigid.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What's that supposed to mean?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Hmph. Forget the Victorian mongrel. What about you?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: You're descended from the Exiled King, from the very clan that's supposed to warn the Tarans of impending Catastrophes—yet here you are, mingling with the likes of him.

spans.text: You're descended from the Exiled King, from the very clan that's supposed to warn the Tarans of impending Catastrophes—yet here you are, mingling with the likes of

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Even during the war, you never cared whether your own people won or lost, you'd just coldly toss those battle reports into the citadel, then go door to door delivering those meaningless personal letters...

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Are you lot even fit to call yourselves Tarans?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: So, this is the only place you have to go? Why not just go back to Culann?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I... I need to wash my clothes first. Should be quick. You don't need to worry about me, Brigid.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Of course I'm worried. I came here just to see you, after all.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hmph. How is a place wrecked by war and left to rot any better than Culann's workshop? At least there you'd have the forge keeping you warm, and hot meals.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: No, it's just that... I don't want to cause him any more trouble. Please—don't tell Culann about what happened today. Okay? I'll be on my way as soon as my clothes dry.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I'm not here for him, Theo. I'm here for you, to take you away.

spans.text: I'm not here for him, Theo. I'm here for

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Take me way? Did he say something to you?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Just what sort of relationship do you have with him, anyway?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: If I hadn't shown up today, were you going to take the beating without fighting back? My instincts are never wrong: if you stay in the city, they'll just keep finding new ways to push you around.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Today, they shoved you into a puddle and beat you with a cane. Tomorrow, who knows?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Anyhow, just come with me. I can take you to the plains, or anywhere else you fancy. Up to you.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You and me, we don't belong here. And if you've got nowhere else to go, you can always head to Nemos's old place and stay with the wakemen for a while.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I do want to see them, after all the stories Nemos has told me...

spans.text: want to see them, after all the stories Nemos has told me...

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: But I can't leave, not unless Culann asks me to.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Nemos has no time to look after him, and the dragon statue isn't finished yet. What would he do if I just up and left?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: But still, thanks Brigid.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: If you say so. Then I'll take you back to the city before I leave.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: No, don't bother. It's cold out, so my clothes won't be dry for a while. I'll go back then.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: And if all else fails, I can always take shelter in that abandoned home. Someone left a quilt and bedsheets there, and I've stayed there before. It'll be fine.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...If you really don't want to come with, well, I suppose it's safer here than risking a trip to another city.

spans.text: don't want to come with, well, I suppose it's safer here than risking a trip to another city.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: So not even Culann looks after you all the time, huh?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: He has more important things to do. I should be making things easier on him, not giving him something else to worry about.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Well, goodbye then. Take care of yourself, you hear?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: We're here!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Like I said, you've come at the perfect time. Today we have fresh ale, stew, and oatmeal... if only we had a bonfire.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Shouldn't you save that for Samhain?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: According to the old customs, we can actually light it a few days before Samhain.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Then again, the war just ended, so we really don't have much in the way of firewood. We can't just start chopping down trees, either, because of the curfew.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: At any rate, it's still light out. The sun can be our bonfire today!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: But that's enough chit-chat—take a seat. I'll have them make room for you.
Loughshinny steps forward. In the damp, chilly air, each dish in the lavish spread on the table has the same familiar scent.
Warm, rustic, and simple, yet not what it seems.
She looks around, concealing her surprise, only to find that no one else finds any of this unusual.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Is this stewed meat?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Yeah. This here is the meat, these are grilled fins, and your cup is full of ale. Oh, right, and we also have oatmeal. I'll go grab you a bowl.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But...
All the dishes appear to be made of the same thing.
They're all made of potatoes, right?
Their statue is bowls. Their bonfire is the sun. Their feast is... potatoes.
As the friendly resident goes to fetch a bowl of 'oatmeal', Loughshinny stands up and walks toward the cart-and-burdenbeast that has been waiting for her the whole time.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Her Highness will return very soon. Please wait here.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: And this place is...?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Na Saoirsí citadel. The highest point in the city is just up the steps beside you. This is also where Her Highness lingers most, when she's in the city.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I'm glad to see you aren't filling the halls with candlelight, musicians, and lavish feasts.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: I've already told you: the primary reason the city is short on supplies is because trade between Victoria and Tara has not yet fully resumed. We're working as hard as we can to resolve the issue.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: The residents are very understanding of the situation. They hold nothing but goodwill and genuine love for Tara.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Your Highness Eblana!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Leave us.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: At once!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Loughshinny.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Just what is going on in this city, Sister?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Everyone's celebrating Samhain, except there's no harvest, no bonfire, and the feast is nothing but potatoes!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: If you came here to make me repeat what the Brigadier has already told you, well, I suppose I can play along. I wouldn't want to spoil our long overdue reunion.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I'm more worried about your spear. Where is it now?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: My spear?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If you're talking about the spear you gave me, it's being stored in a warehouse on Rhodes Island. I no longer need it.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: How can someone with no weapon claim any sort of power? Or forget power—even survival would be a struggle.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I said 'the spear you gave me.'

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Also, you won't kill me. At least, not yet.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: As a puppet that has only just regained its soul, you wouldn't want to break me before you've had a chance to play with your new toy.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Your words are... quite hurtful.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Anyone can be made a puppet, Loughshinny, anyone except you. You are my dance partner, yet you'd rather stand in my shadow than join me on the floor.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Until about a year ago. You finally got bored of me, didn't you?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: ...I don't recall what you're referring to.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: As for power, I'm not here for power. That power rightly belongs to you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: You've been setting fires all across Tara. Those fires have melted the chains that once bound the Tarans. That much is true.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Then why have you returned?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: To bear witness.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If you're truly willing to use your power to give the Tarans a new beginning, then I will do everything I can to support you.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Say, for example, that you're too busy to deal with the supply shortages in the city right now. If so, I would be willing to help with that.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Whether I step forward as a second red dragon, or hide my identity as before, it makes no difference to me.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As noble as ever, my dear sister.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But I can't say whether...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...you would truly be satisfied with that.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The sister I knew wasn't someone who sought power simply to live a life of indulgence. She wanted more than that.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But so far, every step you've taken has been paved with bones and blood.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I can only pray that's because you've had no other choice.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I sincerely hope I will never have reason to collect my spear and come searching for you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Not bad. Not bad at all.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: It seems your life of wandering has taught you far more than you ever learned while acting as my shadow.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Let's not beat around the bush. I've made my intentions clear, and you've invited me back. So what is it you want from me?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You'll find out, soon enough.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Until you do, though, why not come with me? I'll show you around the Red Dragon's Lair.
Legend has it that the architect deliberately shaped the plate with uneven elevations to mirror the old Taran capital.

Legend has it that Tara's stonemasons showcased their finest craftsmanship in every building they made—save for one. They refused to add even a single ornament to the citadel, knowing it would be inhabited by a puppet king.
Loughshinny has heard many stories like this, but no story can tell you whether it is itself a true flame, or merely its shadow cast on the wall.
And so, she follows her sister up the steps and looks down at the city with her own eyes.
She sees the empty pedestal in the square below. It seems to be waiting for something massive to be placed upon it.
She sees the winding, undulating cobblestone roads stretching from the square, and the humble stone houses, so simple they inspire a sense of affection.
But after she focuses her gaze and takes a harder look, she finally sees the thing she had sensed before, the thing that had separated her from the other residents.
It is something that definitely does not belong in the city.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Flames?!
Flames.
At a closer look, there are tiny sparks of fire scattered across the city—all the residents, whether talking, rushing to and fro, yelling, or resting, are surrounded by flickering flames.
Purple flames.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What did you do to these people? You've made them into walking corpses, haven't you?!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You just got back from town. You met them yourself. You should know better than I do.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The flames will spread.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Your flames of death should not be spread to the living.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: It is an unfortunate reality, but wherever man resides, so too does death. Whether on the battlefield or in a bustling city. The flames merely hasten the inevitable.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But I must admit, it doesn't sit right with me either.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The dead wander the wilderness, driven by the desires they held in life. While those tainted by the flames of death can never truly start anew... Life and death cannot remain entangled like this, each defiling the other.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But... haven't you been their chief defiler?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No. Death should be mine to command. I cannot have it expanding beyond the boundaries I set.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Well then, my dear sister, what would you like Tara to become? I want your opinion.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Should the living endure and the dead rest in peace? Or should all of Tara become a kingdom of death?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Why ask a question you already know the answer to?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Then it is clear what you must do.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Kill me, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: While you've been trudging through the crowds, I've been busy preparing.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The moment the tip of your spear pierces my heart, heralding death's embrace, everything tainted by my deathly flames shall leave this realm along with me.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Then, you will become the first and only true leader Tara has seen in decades.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...I will not be your shadow anymore, and we red dragons will not be the monsters they claim us to be—slaughtering our own kin in madness.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Sometimes—often, even—kinslaying can be a virtuous act.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What about those touched by your fire—can they really start their lives anew, as you promised?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I have promised nothing about life, Loughshinny, not even for those untouched by my flames.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As for the cityfolk, they have already been entangled by the violet flames. They will gradually become walking corpses, and eventually leave here with me. This much is certain.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: They are living, breathing people! They fought under your command and won your war for you—they have the right to start anew!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: An unfortunate fate, to be sure, but their fate nonetheless.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No, Eblana. It shall not be their fate.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: What will you do, then?
Loughshinny has more to say, but Eblana has already turned around and started walking down the long corridor. Her footsteps are so soft that Loughshinny did not even realize she had left.
After her sister's figure disappears completely into the darkness, Loughshinny turns her gaze back to the city.
How she wishes it were all just one of Eblana's tricks... but the flames are real.
She clenches her fists, pulls up her hood, and turns to descend the steps.
